CHAPTER V
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
First Part
Institutional

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 16
The Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence is a joint obligation and responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Private Sector and Community Institutions;
c. Society; and
d. Family and/or Parents.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
Region is Dompu Regency. 1. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of Regional autonomy. 2. Regent is the Regent of Dompu. 3. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Dompu Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region. 5. Office hereinafter referred to as PPPA Office is the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Dompu Regency. 6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 7. Woman is a person who is female in gender. 8. Violence is any act against the physical and psychological aspects that is unlawful, with or without using means, that endangers life or the body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence Against Women is any Action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain Actions, coercion, or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any Action or act against a person especially women that results in misery or neglect of the household including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 12. Criminal Act of Sexual Violence hereinafter abbreviated as TPKS is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence and other sexual acts regulated in the Law as long as determined in the Law on Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence. 13. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 14. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 16. Companion is a person or representative from an Institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, advocacy, reintegration for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 17. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss either physical suffering, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or individuals including the victim's heirs. 18. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 19. Outreach is an action to respond to reports of alleged problems of women and children that need to be verified and followed up. 20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life. 21. Coordination is an effort made to realize integration and harmony in the context of services for women and children experiencing problems. 22. Task Force for Handling Women's and Children's Problems hereinafter abbreviated as Satgas PPA is a task force formed to handle women's and children's problems reported to women's and children's service organizations that have been established by the regional government. 23. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women's and Children's Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional Technical Implementation Unit established by the Regional Government in providing Services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 24. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an independent Institution established by the Regent to support supervision of the implementation of child protection in the region. 25. Integrated Community-Based Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as PATBM is a movement of networks or groups of citizens at the community level who work in a coordinated manner to achieve the goals of child protection. 26. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years. 27. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 28. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent and handle criminal acts of human trafficking in Dompu Regency. 29. Task Force for Prevention of Child Marriage is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent child marriage in Dompu Regency. 30.

REGENT OF DOMPU
PROVINCE OF WEST NUSA TENGGARA
REGIONAL REGULATION OF DOMPU REGENCY
NUMBER 02 YEAR 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural, and the social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as an integral part of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens through various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women’s empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected that they will be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen forms of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.
Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, the community, and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The said efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with the aforementioned matters, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as to ensure legal certainty in the implementation of women’s empowerment and the protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 56
(1) Regional Government may establish partnerships with the Business Sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for Women and Child Victims of Acts of Violence, and
b. education and training for Women and Child Victims of Acts of Violence.

REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES
DOMPU REGENCY
REGENT OF DOMPU
DECIDES:
REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government may establish a PPA Task Force in an effort to coordinate the provision of services for Women and Children who are victims of acts of violence.
(2) The PPA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to:
   a. coordinate and synchronize protection services for women and children carried out by the Regional Government, Regional Apparatus/Institutions, and the community;
   b. improve cooperation and referral systems; and collect, compile, and present reports on violence.
(3) The establishment of the PPA Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF DOMPU REGENCY
NUMBER 02 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER IX
MONITORING EVALUATION AND REPORTING
Article 57
(1) Monitoring, evaluation and reporting on the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence includes supervision in preventive, rehabilitative and curative efforts.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted every 3 (three) months.
(3) Evaluation and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted every 6 (six) months.
(4) Monitoring, evaluation and reporting shall be conducted by the agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 37
The Regional Government may provide assistance to women and children victims of violence.
Assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the condition of victims, which are carried out at health service units, education, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts, and social service institutions.
Assistance as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by UPTD PPA assistants and other assistants.

Article 33
(1) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (1) letter e, aim to return victims to be accepted back into their social environment.
(2) Repatriation and social reintegration services for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out after socialization related to the rights of women and children as victims of violence.
(3) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with regional apparatus/related institutions, and the community.

2.4.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation establishes institutions and coordination mechanisms (e.g., UPTD PPA in Pasal 22; possible gugus tugas in Pasal 23; Satgas PPA in Pasal 25; PATBM in Pasal 26; planning via Rencana Aksi Daerah and IKU in Pasal 17). It also states a principle of “keadilan dan kesetaraan gender” (Pasal 2). However, it does not explicitly require or institutionalize “pengarusutamaan gender” (gender mainstreaming) as a cross-cutting institutional mechanism (e.g., mandatory gender analysis, gender-responsive budgeting, gender focal points, mainstreaming across all sectors/programs). The retrieved English candidates accurately reflect this: they show gender equality as a principle and various institutions, but no explicit gender mainstreaming mandate. Therefore the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the actual text, and the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-interprets general gender-equality language as gender mainstreaming institutionalisation.

6.5.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes disability-specific measures within special protection for children (children with disabilities; fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities; accessibility provisions), indicating special protection measures targeted at people with disabilities (at least for children).

6.5.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly includes disability in special protection provisions for children. Pasal 38 ayat (2) lists “Anak Penyandang Disabilitas” as a category receiving “Pelindungan Khusus.” Pasal 39 ayat (3) includes “pemenuhan kebutuhan khusus bagi anak penyandang disabilitas,” and Pasal 40 ayat (1) includes “pemberian aksebilitas, terutama bagi anak penyandang disabilitas.” These are clear disability-specific measures (at least for children). The retrieved English passages contain the same content, and the judge’s ‘Yes’ follows directly. Thus the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect for this policy as written.

Article 11
Other violence as referred to in Article 5 (1) letter g, constitutes threat of violence and coercion. Threat of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes every unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, image, symbol, or body movement, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

6.10.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly mentions refugees/displacement in the child special protection chapter. Pasal 39 ayat (1) huruf a states “Anak yang menjadi pengungsi” under “Pelindungan Khusus kepada Anak dalam Situasi Darurat.” This is a direct reference to refugee status (forced displacement) and is accompanied by a list of protection actions in Pasal 39 ayat (3). The retrieved English candidate passage includes “Children who become refugees,” so the judge’s ‘Yes’ is supported by the source. Therefore the golden label ‘No’ likely reflects a labeling guideline mismatch (e.g., expecting measures for refugees generally, not only children), but based on the document text itself, the policy does address refugees (at least child refugees).
